newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada firm may make film of Bre-X gold saga.
newsitem.headline: Canada firm may make film of Bre-X gold saga.

text.p: The dramatic saga of troubled Canadian gold explorer Bre-X Minerals Ltd. may soon be coming to a movie theater near you.

Toronto-based Alliance Communications Corp. confirmed on Monday a published report that it acquired the film rights to one of the books being written about Calgary, Alberta-based Bre-X, which claimed to have made the century's richest gold find.
Alliance said it signed an option with Canadian journalist Brian Hutchinson to turn his book on Bre-X into a feture-length movie.
"We're just fascinated with the story," an Alliance spokeswoman said.
Hutchinson spent a month researching in Indonesia, wrote a cover story about Bre-X for Canadian Business Magazine and is working on the book.

Bre-X became Canada's most talked about Canadian business story even before doubts emerged last month about whether the tiny exploration company discovered the world's biggest gold reserves in the jungles of Borneo. Results from an independent audit of the property are expected in early May.

Shares of Bre-X plunged on the Toronto Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, wiping billions of dollars from investor portfolios after Bre-X's New Orleans-based partner Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. reported that it found insignificant amounts of gold at Bre-X's Busang site in Borneo.
Bre-X was also rocked by the apparent suicide of its top geologist at Busang, who allegedly jumped to his death from a helicopter, leaving a suicide note for one of his four wives.

The cast of characters runs from Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh, who parlayed his last C$10,000 ($7,150) into a possible bonanza, Freeport's flamboyant Texas-born Chief Executive Jim Bob Moffatt and Indonesian President Suharto.
Another book on Bre-X is also due out from Maclean's magazine writer Jennifer Wells, who may also be pursuing a movie deal.
